page: Microsoft Azure E32s_v7 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The instance provides 32 dedicated virtual CPUs across 16 physical cores via multithreading, backed by a 480 MB L3 cache. It allocates 256.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio tailored for data-dense workloads. The server does not bundle local ephemeral storage, utilizing network-attached block volumes like Azure Premium Storage, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark testing shows consistent middle-tier performance across general multi-threaded compute, recording a PassMark CPU score of 47694.11 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 31862.21. Memory bandwidth throughput reaches 181.75 GB/sec for uncached 256MB reads and 77.85 GB/sec for writes. The platform delivers top-quartile performance in targeted vector and matrix operations due to AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets, demonstrated by a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 35.62 GB/sec and 186.24 tokens per second in 7B model prompt processing.

Without integrated local disks or hardware accelerators, cost efficiency relies heavily on high memory utilization and CPU-bound analytical throughput. The absence of local scratch space requires workloads to direct all storage operations through external block storage. The system configuration is best aligned with in-memory caching tiers, large relational or NoSQL database engines, real-time analytics platforms, and batch data processing.
